la:verb:duco.html:
dūco, xi, ctum, 3 (
imp. duc; but duce,; ; ; ; ; .—Perf. sync.: duxti, Varr. ap. ; ; ), v. a.
cf. Goth. tiuh-an; O. H. Germ. zieh-an, to draw; Germ. -zog, in Herzog, commander, duke
, to lead, conduct, draw, bring forward, in all senses; very freq. passing over into the signif. of the compounds abducere, deducere, adducere, producere, etc., and of the synonyms agere, trahere, movere, etc. (very freq.).
Lit.
In gen.: quo sequar? quo ducis nunc me?: duc hos intro, id. Am. 2, 2, 224; : duc ac demonstra mihi,: suas secum mulierculas sunt in castra ducturi,; cf. et saep.: (difficile iter) vix qua singuli carri ducerentur,; cf. plaustra,: aquam ducere, Cato ap. P.; so, aquam per fundum ejus,: spiritum naribus,: so, spiritum per siccas fauces,; cf.: aërem spiritu,: animam spiritu,; and in gen.: spiritum, for to live, ; cf.: vitam et spiritum,: tura naribus,to inhale,: sucos nectaris,to drink in full draughts, to quaff,; cf. pocula,; and: Liberum,.—Poet.: jucunda oblivia vitae (referring to the waters of Lethe), (cf. ) et saep.: mucronem,to draw from the scabbard,; cf.: ferrum vaginā,: ensem vagina,; but: ensem duxerat faber,had beaten out, forged,: sortem,; ; hence, also transf. of that which is drawn by lot,; ; ; ; : pondus aratri,to draw,: remos,to row,; cf. : numerosa brachia,in dancing,: lanas,to spin,; cf. stamina,: ubera,to milk,: frena manu,to guide, govern,: vela, to haul (= navigare), : manus, of swimming,: ilia,to draw the flanks together, become broken-winded,: os,to draw awry, to make wry faces,; ; cf. vultum,; ; et saep.: non equus impiger Curru ducet Achaico Victorem,to draw along,; cf. .—Absol.: sibi quisque ducere, trahere, rapere,to take to one's self, appropriate,.—
Esp.
To lead, conduct, as a way or road: via ducit (te), in urbem?; cf. ; ; : Brundisium Minuci melius via ducat an Appi,: via ad undas,: via ad infernas sedes,; cf.: iter ad urbem,; ; ; ; ; ; —
Se, in colloq. lang., to betake one's self, go: jam me ad regem recta ducam,; ; ; : Balbus duxit se a Gadibus, Asin. ap. .—
A legal t. t., to take, lead away, drag, carry off a person before court, to prison, to punishment, etc.: POST. DEINDE. MANVS. INIECTIO. ESTO. IN. IVS. DVCITO, XII. Tab. ap. ; so, in jus,: illos duci in carcerem jubent,: aliquem in carcerem,: in vincula,: ad mortem,; ; and absol.: ducite, ubi capiat, etc.,; Sen. de Ira, 1, 16, 14; ; : NI. IVDICATVM. FACIT. AVT. QVIS. ENDO. EM. IVRE. VINDICIT. SECVM. DVCITO. VINCITO, etc., XII. Tab. ap. : decreta ejus modi: SI PETIT DUCAS. C. Fuficium duci jussit petitorem,to be imprisoned,; so of a debtor (addictus) who is led off as a slave, Novat. ap. ; ; ; ; cf. ; cf. prov.: stultitiast venatum ducere invitas canes,. —
Uxorem, to lead a wife home, i. e. to marry: bona uxor si ea deducta est, etc. ... Verum egon eam ducam domum, Quae, etc.?: uxorem domum,; : filiam Orgetorigis in matrimonium,; cf. : eum uxorem ducturum esse aliam,: uxorem (or aliquam, filiam alicujus, etc.),; et saep.; ; et saep.; ; ; ; ; et saep.—Absol.: si tu negaris ducere,; ; ; : jugum ducere cum infidelibus, i. e. to be yoked in marriage, .—Rarely for nubere: si ignorans statum Erotis ut liberum duxisti, isque postea servus est judicatus, etc., Imp. Antonin. ap. .—In the comic poets, of taking home prostitutes, ; ; ; ; et saep.—
In milit. lang.
Said of a commander, to lead, to cause to move, to march his army in any direction: locis apertis exercitum ducere,; cf. ; : exercitum ab Allobrogibus in Segusianos,: exercitum in fines Suessionum,; cf. ; 5, 18, 1: exercitum (legiones, etc.) in Bellovacos,; 5, 24, 2 et saep.; cf. : cohortes ad eam partem munitionum, quae, etc.,: exercitum Uticam,: reliquas copias contra Labienum, et saep.—In pass., of the soldiers, to march, move: quam in partem aut quo consilio ducerentur,.—And in act., absol., of the general himself, to march, move (a favorite expression of Liv.; not in Caes. or Sall.): (Mettus) ducit, quam proxime ad hostem potest,; ; ; 22, 18 et saep.—Hence,
In gen., to lead, command an army or (more freq.) a division: qua in legatione duxit exercitum,; so, exercitum,; : qui superiore anno primum pilum duxerat,; ; : ordinem,; 3, 104, 3; : partem exercitūs, et saep.—Rarely, to lead a division in front, in advance: consuetudine sua Caesar sex legiones expeditas ducebat: post eas ... inde, etc.,; hence also, to march in front, take the lead, said of the division that forms the van: pars equitum et auxiliariae cohortes ducebant, mox prima legio, etc.,; cf. fin.—
Transf. beyond the milit. sphere, to lead, to be leader, head, chief, first in any thing: accedit etiam, quod familiam ducit, Manut.; so, familiam,; : ordines,: classem (discipulorum), Spald.: funus,: toros, et saep.—
To conduct as prisoners in a triumph: per triumphum,: in triumpho,, v. triumphus.—
With the accessory idea of creation, formation, to produce, form, construct, make, fashion, shape, dispose (cf.: struo, pono, condo, fundo): parietem per vestibulum alicujus,to erect,; cf. muros,: vallum ex castris ad aquam,: fossam,; : arcum,: lateres de terra,: vivos vultus de marmore (with excudere spirantia aera),; cf. ; ; Varr. ap. ; ; Spald.; ; hence, poet. also: epos,: carmen,; : versus, et saep.: liniam ex colore,; ; cf. orbem,: alvum,to bring forth by clysters,; et saep.: alapam alicui, qs. to fetch one a box on the ear, ; cf. colaphum, Spald.: pugnum, et saep.; so esp. of processions, dances, etc.: funus,; ; ; cf. exsequias,: pompam,; ; : choros,; ; et saep.; cf. choreas,; .—
To receive, admit, take any thing (not ante-Aug.): cicatricem,; : rimam,: situm,to grow rusty,: formam,: colorem,; cf. pallorem,to grow pale,: nomina,: notam, et saep.
Trop.
In gen., to lead, guide, draw, conduct: progredimur quo ducit quemque voluntas,; cf. ; : ad strepitum citharae cessatum ducere curam,: Liber vota bonos ducit ad exitus,; cf. : per quaedam parva sane ducant (futurum oratorem),; cf. ; .—Prov.: ducunt volentem fata, nolentem trahunt,.—
In partic.
To draw, deduce,

derive its origin or beginning from, any thing: ab aliqua re totius vitae ducere exordium,; cf.: exordium a nostra persona,; : principium disputationis a principe investigandae veritatis,: belli initium a fame,; cf. : initia causasque omnium ex quatuor temporum mutationibus,: originem ab Isocrate,; ; : ingressionem non ex oratoriis disputationibus, sed, etc.,: honestum ab iis rebus,; : nomen ex quo,; cf.: nomen a Graeco,; ; et saep.; cf. also: utrumque (sc. amor et amicitia) ductum (al. dictum) est ab amando,; .—

To lead a person, as regards his will or opinions, in any direction; to move, incite, induce, allure, in a good or bad sense (most freq. in the pass.): ita me ad credendum tua ducit oratio,: nos ducit scholarum consuetudo,; ; cf. : ducit te species, et saep.: declamatores quosdam perversa ducit ambitio, ut, etc.,.—In the pass.: si quis statuarum honore aut gloria ducitur,: eloquentiae laude,: quaestu et lucro,: hoc errore ut, etc.,; cf.: litteris eorum et urbanitate, ut, etc.,: omnes trahimur et ducimur ad cognitionis et scientiae cupiditatem, et saep.—
In a bad sense, to cheat, deceive, ; ; ; ; (3, 8, 1 M.); ; (with decipere).—
With regard to time, to draw out, extend, protract, prolong: bellum,; ; sq.; ; et saep.; cf.: bellum longius,; : bellum in hiemem,: eam rem longius,; cf.: rem prope in noctem,: rem leniter, et saep. Also transf., of time itself: tempus,; : diem ex die,; and of persons who are put off, delayed: ubi se diutius duci intellexit,.—Less freq. (mostly poet.),
In gen., of time, to pass, spend, enjoy: aetatem in litteris,; so, aetatem,: vitam,; ; cf. (where, shortly before, vitam producere): noctes,; : somnos,.—
In mercant. lang., to calculate, compute, reckon: age nunc summam sumptus duc, Lucil. ap. : minimum ut sequamur, quoniam XC. medimnūm milia duximus, accedant eo, etc.,; and 16; 6, 2, 7; ; .—
Transf. beyond the mercant. sphere.
Rationem alicujus, to consider, calculate, care for one's advantage or interest (a favorite expression of Cicero): duxi meam rationem, quam tibi facile me probaturum arbitrabar, D, § 7; so, suam quoque rationem,to have respect to one's own advantage,; and: non minorem aratorum quam populi rationem,: salutis meae rationem,: rationem officii, non commodi,; cf. : unius cujusque temporis ducta ratio est,: rationem officii atque existimationis,.—
In gen., to reckon, consider, hold, account, esteem as any thing (cf. aestimo and existimo; very freq. in prose and poetry): parvi id ducebat,: pro nihilo aliquid,; ; ; cf. : ea pro falsis ducit,; cf.: innocentiam pro malevolentia,: vos eritis judices, Laudin' an vitio duci id factum oportuit,; so, aliquid honori,: aliquid laudi, Nep. praef. § 4: aliquem despicatui,: nihil praeter virtutem in bonis ducere (for which, shortly after, in bonis habere = numerare), ; aliquem in numero hostium,; ; cf. ; without in, ; cf.: aliquem loco affinium, Kritz. N. cr.: aliquid testimonii loco, : tutelae nostrae duximus, cum Africo bello urgerentur,; cf.: officii duxit exorare filiae patrem, etc.,: faceret, quod e republica fideque sua duceret, et saep.: malum cum amici tuum ducis malum,; cf.: Archytas iracundiam seditionem quandam animi vere ducebat,: eorum, quos idoneos ducebat, consilium habet,: nil rectum nisi quod placuit sibi ducunt,.— With acc. and inf.: sic equidem ducebam animo rebarque futurum,: ut omnia tua in te posita esse ducas humanosque casus virtute inferiores putes,; ; ; ; 3, 9 (three times); ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—Here too probably belongs the much disputed passage: ludos et inania honoris medio rationis atque abundantiae duxit (= ludos publicos cum aliis rebus quae ad inania honoris pertinent, duxit, i. e. existimavit habendos et ponendos in medio rationis atque abundantiae, ut inter rationem, quae plane spernit inania, et abundantiam, quae eadem ostentat, media via incederet), he thought right to manage them in a middle course between reason and profusion, , v. Dübner and Orell. ad h. l.

la:conj:dum.html:
dum,
conj. [for dium, acc. from dius; cf. diu, Corss. Ausspr. 2, 856], denotes the temporal relation of two actions to cach other,
As contemporaneous, or,
As in immediate succession, so that with the commencement of one action the other ceases.
As contemporaneous.
Without respect to the limits of the two actions, while, whilst, during the time in which.
In gen., construed with the indicative, except in oratio obliqua, where the subjunctive was sometimes used. In Aug. poets and late prose the subjunctive often stands in oratio directa, v. the following).
Indic. praes.: dum cum hac usuraria Uxore mihi nunc morigero, haec curata sint Fac sis,; so ; ; ; ; ; et saep.— In the praes. histor.: dum haec loquimur, interea loci ad macellum ubi advenimus, etc.,; ; ; : dum haec geruntur, Caesari nuntiatum est, etc.,; cf. these forms of transition,; 4, 32, 1; 4, 34, 3; 5, 22, 1; 6, 7, 1; 7, 57, 1; ; et saep. dum ea conquiruntur et conferuntur, nocte intermissa circiter hominum milia VI ad Rhenum contenderunt, ; cf. ; ; ; .—In the imperf.: dum haec in Appulia gerebantur, Samnites ... urbem non tenuerunt,; ; ; ; ; cf.: dum is in aliis rebus erat occupatus,—In the fut.; nunc animum advortite Dum argumentum hujus eloquar comoediae, .—In the perf.: dum Cyri et Alexandri similis esse voluit, Crassorum inventus est dissimillimus,; so ; ; ; ; —In the pluperf.: dum in unam partem oculos animosque hostium certamen averterat, pluribus locis scalis capitur murus,.—In the fut. perf.: bellum ingens geret Italia... Tertia dum Latio regnantem viderit aestas,.—Prov.: dum loqueris,i. e. this instant,.—In the oratio obliqua: dic, hospes, Spartae, nos te hic vidisse jacentes, Dum sanctis patriae legibus obsequimur, Poëta ap. ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—
Subj. In oratio obliqua: dixisti, dum Planci in me meritum verbis extollerem, me arcem facere e cloaca,; so ; ; ; ; al.—In oratio recta: o quotiens ausae, caneret dum valle sub alta, Rumpere mugitu carmina docta boves,: dum intentus in eum se rex totus averteret, etc.,: dum ea in Samnio gererentur,; ; ; ; ; ; ; —
When the principal action is an immediate and sudden sequence of that described in

the clause with dum, subito or repente is often used in the principal clause: dum tempus teritur, repente milites, etc.,: dum advenientes filia interrogat, repente in osculis, etc. : dum Appium orno, subito sum factus accusatoris ejus socer,; .—

When the actions are simply presented as contemporaneous, interea, jam or interea jam is often used in the principal clause: dum haec mecum reputo, accersitur lavatum interea virgo,; : dum ea Romani parant, jam Saguntum oppugnabatur,; cf. also: dum ... interim,; ; —
Esp., of duration in the present, now, yet.
In combination with etiam primum, and esp. freq. with the negations non, nec, ne, haud, nihil, nullus, nemo, v. h vv.—
Colloq., as an enclitic with imperatives and interjections (by some separately written ades dum, abi dum, etc, but v. Ritschl, Opusc Phil p. 567 sq.), orig, acc of time, a moment, a second, a little Sosia adesdum, paucis te volo, abidum, circumspicedum, Plaut Trin. 1, 2, 109: dicdum, facitodum, iteradum, Poëta ap. jubedum, : manedum,; : memoradum,: tacedum,: tangedum,: agedum (most freq.),; ; ; et saep. (for which, agidum, Ritschl ad loc.); ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; : agitedum, Drak.; 5, 52; 7, 34 fin.: cedodum,: ehodum,; ; ; ; also in Plaut. in enumerations: primumdum (= Gr. πρῶτον μέν), ; ; —
With respect to the temporal limit of both actions, i. q. tamdiu quam or usque eo, as long as, while.
Lit. (with indic. when the duration of the action in the principal clause is alone implied, except in the oratio obliqua).—In praes.: bene factum a vobis, dum vivitis, non abscedet, Cato ap. ; so ; ; ; al.—In fut.: quid illos opinamini animi habuisse atque habituros, dum vivent? Cato ap. ; ; ; ; et saep.—
Subj., often, when the clause with dum expresses a desired end, or refers to an indefinite future: non tibi venit in mentem, Si, dum vivas, tibi bene facias, etc.,: pars, dum vires suppeterent, eruptionem censebant,: ut sua sponte, dum sine periculo liceret, excederet Gadibus,: hoc unum esse tempus de pace agendi, dum sibi uterque confideret ut pares ambo viderentur,: de quo (sc. animo) dum disputarem, tuam mihi dari vellem, Cotta, eloquentiam, Bait. (v. Roby, Gram. 2, 284 sq.). —
With tamdiu, tantum, tantummodo, tantisper, usque; or opp. postea, postquam, deinde, ubi, nunc, etc.—With tamdiu, ; ; ; ; —With tantum, .—With tantummodo, .—With tantisper, ; ; .—With usque, : dum ... postea, —dum ... postea quam, ; —dum ... postquam, ; ; cf. —dum ... deinde, ; —dum ... sed ubi, ; —dum ... nunc, ; .—For tamdiu ... dum, less freq. dum ... dum, as long as ... so long: sic virgo dum intacta manet, dum cara suis, and 56; cf. : dum habeat, dum amet, (al. tum).—
In Plautus repeatedly with an emphatic quidem, ; ; ; ; .—
Transf.
In conditional relations as a restrictive particle, like quatenus and duntaxat, so long as, if so be that, provided that, if only (so regularly connected with the subjunctive; freq. in prose and poetry): dum pereas, nihil interduo aiant vivere,: Ly. Concede, inspiciam quid sit scriptum. Cu. Maxime, Tuo arbitratu, dum auferam abs te id quod peto, ; cf.: dum res maneant, verba fingant arbitratu suo,: oderint, dum metuant, Att. ap. : licet lascivire, dum nihil metuas, et saep.; in the imperf.: qui sese in cruciatum dari cuperet, dum de patris morte quaereretur,; ; ; : An. Non pudet vanitatis? Do. Minime, dum ob rem, ; so without a verb,; ; ; ; ; cf.: dum eatenus,.—
With an emphatic modo, and often in one word, dummodo: aeque istuc facio dummodo Eam des, quae sit quaestuosa, etc.,; ; ; ; ; ; ; (4, 16, 17 M.); ; cf.: sin autem jejunitatem ... dummodo sit polita, dum urbana, dum elegans, in Attico genere ponit, etc.,: dummodo sit dives, barbarus ille placet,.—Separated by other words: mea nil refert, dum patiar modo,: certumst pati, dum illum modo habeam mecum,; .—
With tamen, and, in Plautus (cf. above, 1. c.), with quidem.—With tamen, ; ; ; ; ; .—With quidem, ; ; cf. the foll. number.—
In negative conditional clauses, with ne, so long as not, provided that not, if only not: VTEI. SENATVS. NOSTER. DECERNERET. DVM. NE. MINVS. SENATORIBVS. C. ADESENT., S. C. de Bac. (thrice): id faciat saepe, dum ne lassus fiat,; ; cf. ; ; ; ; , B fin.; Drak.; 28, 40; .—So too, dummodo ne, ; ; ; : dum quidem ne,.—
With a causal accessory notion, until, long enough for, etc (very rare, only with subjunctive) obsidio deinde per paucos dies magis quam oppugnatio fuit, dum vulnus ducis curaretur, Liv 21, 8; cf. ; nam se quoque moveri finget, dum aditum sibi ad aures faciat, .
In immediate suceession, until, until that (with the subjunctive or the indicative, as the idea of aim or simply of time predominates; cf. e.g.: quid dicam, quantus amor bestiarum sit in educandis custodiendisque iis, quae procreaverunt, usque ad eum finem, dum possint se ipsa defendere?: ea mansit in condicione atque pacto usque ad eum finem, dum judices rejecti sunt,; cf. ; ; ; . Cicero generally, Caesar always employs the subjunctive).
Subj.: is dum veniat, sedens ibi opperibere,; cf.: paulisper mane, dum edormiscat unum somnum,; cf. also ; so with exspectare,; ; ; : ; ; et saep.; with morari,; ; ; cf. infra, β: sic deinceps omne opus contexitur, dum justa muri altitudo expleatur,; ; cf.: multa quoque et bello passus, dum conderet urbem Inferretque deos Latio,: ut spatium intercedere posset, dum milites convenirent, legatis respondit, etc.,: Caesar ex eo tempore, dum ad flumen Varum veniatur, se frumentum daturum pollicetur, from that time until, etc., : differant in tempus aliud, dum defervescat ira, (cf. ib.: dum se ipsi colligant): quippe qui moram temporis quaererent, dum Hannibal in Africam traiceret, et saep.—
Indic.: tu hic nos, dum eximus, interea opperibere,; so with opperiri,; with manere aliquem,; with exspectare,; with morari,; cf.: causas innecte morandi, Dum pelago desaevit hiems,: retine, dum ego huc servos evoco,; cf.: Tityre, dum redeo, pasce capellas,: struppis, quibus lectica deligata erat, usque adeo verberari jussit, dum animam efflavit, Gracch. ap. ; cf. in the perf., ; in the fut., . See Hand, Turs. II. pp. 303-330.

senses: emphatic, expresses surprize, impatience, indefiniteness, etc; yet, now

With tamdiu, tantum, tantummodo, tantisper, usque; or opp. postea, postquam, deinde, ubi, nunc, etc.—With tamdiu, ; ; ; ; —With tantum, .—With tantummodo, .—With tantisper, ; ; .—With usque, : dum ... postea, —dum ... postea quam, ; —dum ... postquam, ; ; cf. —dum ... deinde, ; —dum ... sed ubi, ; —dum ... nunc, ; .—For tamdiu ... dum, less freq. dum ... dum, as long as ... so long: sic virgo dum intacta manet, dum cara suis, and 56; cf. : dum habeat, dum amet, (al. tum).—
In Plautus repeatedly with an emphatic quidem, ; ; ; ; .—
Transf.
In conditional relations as a restrictive particle, like quatenus and duntaxat, so long as, if so be that, provided that, if only (so regularly connected with the subjunctive; freq. in prose and poetry): dum pereas, nihil interduo aiant vivere,: Ly. Concede, inspiciam quid sit scriptum. Cu. Maxime, Tuo arbitratu, dum auferam abs te id quod peto, ; cf.: dum res maneant, verba fingant arbitratu suo,: oderint, dum metuant, Att. ap. : licet lascivire, dum nihil metuas, et saep.; in the imperf.: qui sese in cruciatum dari cuperet, dum de patris morte quaereretur,; ; ; : An. Non pudet vanitatis? Do. Minime, dum ob rem, ; so without a verb,; ; ; ; ; cf.: dum eatenus,.—
With an emphatic modo, and often in one word, dummodo: aeque istuc facio dummodo Eam des, quae sit quaestuosa, etc.,; ; ; ; ; ; ; (4, 16, 17 M.); ; cf.: sin autem jejunitatem ... dummodo sit polita, dum urbana, dum elegans, in Attico genere ponit, etc.,: dummodo sit dives, barbarus ille placet,.—Separated by other words: mea nil refert, dum patiar modo,: certumst pati, dum illum modo habeam mecum,; .—
With tamen, and, in Plautus (cf. above, 1. c.), with quidem.—With tamen, ; ; ; ; ; .—With quidem, ; ; cf. the foll. number.—
In negative conditional clauses, with ne, so long as not, provided that not, if only not: VTEI. SENATVS. NOSTER. DECERNERET. DVM. NE. MINVS. SENATORIBVS. C. ADESENT., S. C. de Bac. (thrice): id faciat saepe, dum ne lassus fiat,; ; cf. ; ; ; ; , B fin.; Drak.; 28, 40; .—So too, dummodo ne, ; ; ; : dum quidem ne,.—
With a causal accessory notion, until, long enough for, etc (very rare, only with subjunctive) obsidio deinde per paucos dies magis quam oppugnatio fuit, dum vulnus ducis curaretur, Liv 21, 8; cf. ; nam se quoque moveri finget, dum aditum sibi ad aures faciat, .
In immediate suceession, until, until that (with the subjunctive or the indicative, as the idea of aim or simply of time predominates; cf. e.g.: quid dicam, quantus amor bestiarum sit in educandis custodiendisque iis, quae procreaverunt, usque ad eum finem, dum possint se ipsa defendere?: ea mansit in condicione atque pacto usque ad eum finem, dum judices rejecti sunt,; cf. ; ; ; . Cicero generally, Caesar always employs the subjunctive).
Subj.: is dum veniat, sedens ibi opperibere,; cf.: paulisper mane, dum edormiscat unum somnum,; cf. also ; so with exspectare,; ; ; : ; ; et saep.; with morari,; ; ; cf. infra, β: sic deinceps omne opus contexitur, dum justa muri altitudo expleatur,; ; cf.: multa quoque et bello passus, dum conderet urbem Inferretque deos Latio,: ut spatium intercedere posset, dum milites convenirent, legatis respondit, etc.,: Caesar ex eo tempore, dum ad flumen Varum veniatur, se frumentum daturum pollicetur, from that time until, etc., : differant in tempus aliud, dum defervescat ira, (cf. ib.: dum se ipsi colligant): quippe qui moram temporis quaererent, dum Hannibal in Africam traiceret, et saep.—
Indic.: tu hic nos, dum eximus, interea opperibere,; so with opperiri,; with manere aliquem,; with exspectare,; with morari,; cf.: causas innecte morandi, Dum pelago desaevit hiems,: retine, dum ego huc servos evoco,; cf.: Tityre, dum redeo, pasce capellas,: struppis, quibus lectica deligata erat, usque adeo verberari jussit, dum animam efflavit, Gracch. ap. ; cf. in the perf., ; in the fut., . la:verb:dubito.gloss: to waver (in opinion), be uncertain, doubt, question, be in doubt

la:verb:dubito.html:
dŭbĭto, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. freq. n. and a. [for duhibitare, freq. from duhibeo, i. e. duohabeo (cf. habitare from habeo), to have or hold, as two, v. dubius; cf. also Gr. δοιάζω from δοιοί; Germ. zweifeln from zwei], to vibrate from one side to the other, to and fro, in one's opinions or in coming to a conclusion (freq. in all periods and sorts of composition; in class. prose usually with negations or in a negative interrogation, as: non dubito, haud dubito, quis dubitat? etc.
To waver in opinion or judgment, to be uncertain, to be in doubt, to doubt, question.
Absol. (rare but class.): ne vinolenti quidem quae faciunt eadem approbatione faciunt qua sobrii; dubitant, haesitant, revocant se interdum,; cf. : et interrogamus et dubitamus et affirmamus,; cf. ; : Livius frequentissime dubitat,; : vivo equidem, ne dubita; nam vera vides,: ut jam liceat una comprehensione omnia complecti non dubitantemque (= sine ulla dubitatione) dicere,; Madv.; so .—
With de (class.): de indicando dubitat,; ; ; .—With a negation: nec vero de hoc quisquam dubitare posset, nisi, etc.,: de aliqua re,: de divina ratione,: de tua erga me voluntate,; cf. : de ejus fide,: cf. ; 1, 40 fin.: de carminibus,: de ultima illa (parte),: de se, Pompei ap. A et saep.—Pass. impers.: de armis dubitatum est,: de judicio Panaetii dubitari non potest,; so, de auctore, : de hac (virtute) nihil dubitabitur,.—
With acc. (in class. prose only with a neutr. pron.): haec non turpe est dubitare philosophos, quae ne rustici quidem dubitant?; ; ; ; ; .—In the pass.: causa prorsus, quod dubitari posset, nihil habebat,; cf. ; : dubitati tecta parentis,: sidera,: ne auctor dubitaretur,; cf. infra, ε: dicta haud dubitanda,.—
With an interrog. pron. (good prose, but rare): ubi tu dubites, quid sumas potissimum,: non dubito, quid nobis agendum putes,; ; ; : cur dubitas, quid de re publica sentias?; cf. fin.; —(ε) With interrog. particles (very freq. and class.): si me non improbissime tractasset, dubitassem fortasse utrum, etc.,: desinite dubitare, utrum sit utilius, etc. . . . an, etc.,; cf. impers., ; : honestumne factu sit an turpe dubitant,: dubitavi, hos homines emerem, an non emerem,; cf. ; : recte necne, etc.,: licet et dubitare num quid nos fugerit,: dubito, num, etc.,; ; de L. Bruto fortasse dubitarim, an, etc., et saep.—Cf. respecting the expression dubito an, the art. an, II., and Zumpt, Gramm. § 354.—Poet. in pass. (cf. supra, γ): an dea sim, dubitor,.—(ζ) Non dubito, quin (very freq. and class.): non hercle dubito, quin tibi ingenio nemo praestiterit,; ; ; ; ; : numquid tu dubitas quin ego nunc perpetuo perierim? Have you a doubt? etc., ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; cf. pass. impers.: dubitari (non) potest, quin, etc.,; ; : dubitari potest quin usque eo eicienda sit,: illud cave dubites, quin, etc.,; quid dubitas, quin sit, etc.,; so in an interrog.,; ; ; cf. ; .—(η) With acc. and inf. (freq. only since the Aug. period, and in gen. only negatively; not found in Plaut., Ter., or Cic.; but usual in Nepos): neque humorem dubitavi aurasque perire,: gratos tibi esse qui de me rumores afferuntur, non dubito, (cf., on the contrary, § 7: noli dubitare, quin te sublevaturus sim): ignorabant aut dubitabant animas hominum immortales esse,: non dubito, fore plerosque qui, etc., Nep. praef. § 1; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; Drak. et saep.; ; ; ; et saep.; cf. in an interrog.: an est quisquam qui dubitet, tribunos offensos esse?; so, quis dubitat,; ; . —Pass. impers.: an dubitabitur, ibi partes oratoris esse praecipuas? id. prooem. § 12. —Affirm.: piraticam ut musicam, fabricam dici adhuc dubitabant mei praeceptores, .—
Transf., of inan. and abstr. subjects, to be uncertain, doubtful: si tardior manus dubitet,: suspensa ac velut dubitans oratio,: aut vincere aut, si fortuna dubitabit (= adversabit), etc.,: nec mox fama dubitavit, cum, etc.,.—
Meton., to reflect upon, to ponder, consider, deliberate: in utramque partem cogitare, deliberare, etc. (very rare): haec dum dubitas, menses abierunt decem,: restat, judices, ut hoc dubitemus, uter, etc.,: percipe porro, quid dubitem,: dubitaverat Augustus Germanicum rei Romanae imponere,had considered whether he should,.
To waver in coming to a conclusion, to be irresolute; to hesitate, delay.
With inf. (so most commonly): non dubitaverim

me gravissimis tempestatibus obvium ferre, ; so with a negation,; ; et saep.; : flumen transire, 6, 8, 1; ; and fin.; ; et saep.: quid dubitamus pultare atque huc evocare ambos foras?; so in an interrog.,; ; ; ; ; ; —Very seldom affirmatively: quod ea illi nubere dubitabat,: accusat fratrem, quod dubitet omnia quae ad beatam vitam pertineant ventre metiri,: dubitat agnoscere matrem,: si forte dubitaret quod afferretur accipere,: isdem mandatum ut occiderent, si venire dubitaret,.—Ellipt.: quod dubitas, ne feceris,.—

Non dubito quin (rare in Cic. and Caes.): nemo dubitabat, quin, etc.,; ; : tum dubitandum non existimavit, quin proficisceretur,; ; cf.: nolite dubitare, quin huic uni credatis omnia,; and in an interrog.: dubitabitis, judices, quin? etc.,; .—
Absol. (rare): te neque umquam dubitasse, neque timuisse,: sed mora damnosa est, nec res dubitare remittit,: quid igitur ego dubito?; so in an interrog.,; ; : magnitudine supplicii dubitantes cogit,; ; : dubitantia lumina,failing,. —Hence,
dŭbĭtanter, adv. *
Doubtingly: sine ulla affirmatione, dubitanter unum quodque dicemus,.—
Hesitatingly, with hesitancy (very rare): illum verecunde et dubitanter recepisse,; cf. Asin. Pollio ap. .—
dŭbĭ-tātim, adv. (i. q. dubitanter, 2.), hesitatingly, with hesitation (only in the foll. passages), Sisenn. ap. ; so Cael. Ann. ib.

In poets, like the Gr. διπλοῦς, of character, qs. double-tongued, double-faced, i. e. false, deceitful: Ulixes,: Amathusia,; so, animo,; .—Adv.: dū^-plĭcĭter, doubly, on two accounts, ; ; : res conscriptae,ambiguously,; .

dŭbĭtātĭo, ōnis, f.
dubito

Prop.
In gen. (freq. and good prose).

B. 2. b. ε), ; ; ; ; so too, sine dubitatione, (but far more freq. in signif. II., v.infra).—
With gen.: omnem dubitationem adventus legionum expellere, ; cf. juris (i. e. dubitatio, penes quem esset jus),: generum,: hujus utilitatis,.—

Esp., as a fig. of speech, i. q. Gr. διαπόρησις, i. e. hesitation, embarrassment of the speaker, because unable to do justice to the greatness of his theme (e. g. ; ), ; cf. Ernest. Lex. Technol. Lat. p. 136.—

A wavering, hesitating in coming to a conclusion; hesitancy, irresolution, delay: aestuabat dubitatione, versabat se in utramque partem non solum mente, verum etiam corpore,; cf.: qui timor! quae dubitatio! quanta haesitatio tractusque verborum!: inter dubitationem et moras senati,; cf. : aluit dubitatione bellum, et saep.: (Caesar) nulla interposita dubitatione legiones ex castris educit,without any hesitation, promptly,; in this signif. very freq. in Cicero: sine ulla dubitatione,; ; ; fin.; ; ; , b. 2. et saep.; cf.: absque ulla dubitatione,; less freq. merely sine dubitatione,without hesitation, unhesitatingly,; ; ; ; ; so ; Auct. Trop., vacillating in mind, uncertain.
Act.
Wavering in opinion, doubting, doubtful, dubious, uncertain, = ambigens, haesitans, etc.: sin est is homo, anni multi me dubiam dant,: quae res est, quae cujusquam animum in hac causa dubium facere possit?.— With an interrog. clause, A. and S. Gr. § 213 R. 4 (1.): temptat dubiam mentem rationis egestas, ecquae nam fuerit mundi genitalis origo,; cf.: equites procul visi ab dubiis, quinam essent,: dubius sum, quid faciam,: dubius, unde rumperet silentium,: spemque metumque inter dubii, seu vivere credant, Sive extrema pati,; cf. : Philippus non dubius, quin, etc.,: haud dubius quin,; .—With acc. and inf.: dictator minime dubius, bellum cum his populis Patres jussuros,; so, haud dubius,; : nec sum animi dubius, verbis ea vincere magnum Quam sit,well aware how hard it is,; so, dubius with the genitives animi, Auct. B. Alex. 56, 2: mentis,: consilii,: sententiae, Drak.: salutis,: vitae,: fati,; cf. Zumpt, Gr. § 437; A. and S. Gr. § 213 R. 1 (a.).—
Wavering in resolution, irresolute, undecided (very rare): dubio atque haesitante Jugurtha incolumes transeunt,; cf. hostes (opp. firmi),fin.: nutantes ac dubiae civitates,: quid faciat dubius,.—Poet. transf.: cuspis,.—
Pass., that isdoubted of, uncertain, doubtful, dubious, undetermined (so most freq. in all periods and kinds of composition): videsne igitur, quae dubia sint, ea sumi pro certis atque concessis?; cf. fin.; ; ; ; ; : nihil aegrius est quam res secernere apertas Ab dubiis, (cf. verba, vague language, opp. aperta, ): jus, opp. certum,; opp. confessum,: in regno, ubi ne obscura quidem est aut dubia servitus,: dubium vel anceps genus causarum,; cf. : dubii variique casus, Auct. ap. : et incerta societas, et saep.: quia sciebam dubiam esse fortunam scenicam, prol. alt. 8: salus (opp. aperta pernicies),: spes pacis,: victoria,; cf.: victoria, praeda, laus,: Marte,: spes armorum,: discrimen pugnae,indecisive,: proelia,: auctor,unknown, et saep.: an auspicia repetenda, ne quid dubiis diis agerem?i. e. unassured of their favor,: dubii socii suspensaeque ex fortuna fidei (opp. fideles socii and certi hostes),; cf. : Hispaniae,; cf.: gens dubiae ad id voluntatis,: lux,i. e. morning twilight, dawn,: sidera,; cf. nox,evening twilight,: caelum,i. e. over cast,: fulgor solis,; cf.: et quasi languidus dies,: dubiāque tegens lanugine malas,i. e. between down and a beard,; ; cf.: dubia lanuginis umbra, Pall. et Cel. 42: vina,not sure to ripen,: consilia,wavering, et saep.: hunc annum sequitur annus haud dubiis consulibus (shortly thereafter the contrary: Papirius Semproniusque, quorum de consulatu dubitabatur),; so, haud dubius praetor,: haud dubii hostes,open enemies,: haud dubii Galli (opp. degeneres, mixti, Gallograeci vere),: cena dubia, see below, II.—
In the neutr. absol.
(Non, haud) dubium est, it is (not, not at all) doubtful, uncertain, undecided. (αα) Absol.: si quid erit dubium,: haud dubium id quidem est,; ; cf. in the interrog.: o! dubiumne id est?; ; ; and with the dat.: an dubium id tibi est?; .—(ββ) With de: de Pompeii exitu mihi dubium numquam fuit,; so, de eorum jure,: de re,; cf. .—(γγ) With an interrog. clause: illud dubium (est), ad id, quod summum bonum dicitis, ecquaenam fieri possit accessio,; cf. : hoc ergo, credo, dubium est, uter nostrum sit verecundior,: hoc enim dubium est, utrum ... an,: Ambiorix copias suas judicione non conduxerit ... an tempore exclusus, dubium est,: an dubium vobis fuit inesse vis aliqua videretur necne? et saep.—Since the Aug. per. freq. dubium, absol. and adv.: codicilli, dubium ad quem scripti,: quo postquam dubium pius an sceleratus, Orestes venerat,; ; ; ; ; : Erechtheus, Justitiā dubium validisne potentior armis,; cf. : neque multo post exstincto Maximo, dubium an quaesita morte,; ; —(δδ) Non dubium est quin uxorem nolit filius, ; ; ; ; et saep.: haud dubium est, quin,; ; ; and interrog.,; . —(εε) With acc. and inf.: periisso me una haud dubium est,; so ; ; cf. interrog.: an dubium tibi est, eam esse hanc?.—Ellipt.: si exploratum tibi sit posse te, etc., non esse cunctandum: si dubium sit, non esse conandum,.—
Dubium habere, to regard as uncertain, to doubt: an tu dubium habebis, etiam sancte quom jurem tibi?: an dubium habetis, num obficere quid vobis possit? etc., Dietsch; cf.: haec habere dubia, neque, etc., —
In dubium: in dubium vocare,to call in question,; cf.: illud me dixisse nemo vocabit in dubium, Asin. Pollio ap. . Vid. also under 3. b.: venire in dubium,; ; ; cf.: alii non veniunt in dubium de voluntate,i. e. there is no doubt what their wish is,. Vid. also under 3. b.—
In dubio, in doubt, in question, undetermined: dum in dubio est animus,; cf. : in dubioque fuere utrorum ad regna cadendum esset, etc.,; cf. ; : aestate potius quam hieme dandum, non est in dubio, et saep.: ut in dubio poneret, utrum ... an, etc.,.
